paras: The killing of Thomas at Yorktown, Texas, was the fatal shooting of a Black man described as an escaped convict on the morning of July 31, 1900, by a man the Houston Daily Post identified as Deputy Sheriff Farris. A justice's inquest accepted the shooter's account that Thomas had come at him with a razor, and two Texas papers carried brief dispatches on the case.
According to the Bryan Morning Eagle, Jesse Faris had been robbed of valuables worth $10 or $11 on the night of Monday, July 30.

The two dispatches describe the shooting differently, though both give only the shooter's version. In the Houston Post account, Thomas refused to surrender to the officer and drew a razor, and Farris fired after ordering him several times to halt. The Bryan Eagle said instead that Faris found "a negro convict in the bushes near the creek" and proposed to search him for the stolen property, and that the man came at him with a razor before Faris shot him. The shot was fired about 9 o'clock, and the ball passed through the man's heart, killing him instantly.

Justice Kilgore held an inquest the same day, and "a verdict according to above facts was rendered." Farris' bond had not been fixed, and an examining trial was expected on August 1. No report of the examining trial or its result appears in the coverage.

The case drew only brief notice in Texas white papers: the Houston Daily Post ran a Yorktown dispatch on August 1 under the headline "Negro Killed by an Officer," and the Bryan Morning Eagle printed a separate dispatch on August 2 headed "Killed an Escaped Convict." Neither paper questioned the shooter's account or quoted any other witness, and the Bryan Eagle did not name the dead man at all. No coverage in the Black press was found.
The Houston Post called the shooter a deputy sheriff acting to take an escaped convict, while the Bryan Eagle gave him no title and presented him as a robbery victim searching a suspect.

bases: The Houston Post names the shooter as Deputy Sheriff Farris acting to take an escaped convict (A1); the Bryan Eagle gives him no title and presents him as a robbery victim searching a suspect (A2), so the officer character rests on A1.

Two separately worded Yorktown dispatches agree that a Black convict was shot dead near Yorktown by a man named Farris or Faris after allegedly coming at him with a razor (A1, A2), though both relay only the shooter's account.

accounts.label: Houston Post dispatch (officer's version)
accounts.gist: Thomas, an escaped convict, refused to surrender to Deputy Sheriff Farris and drew a razor; after several orders to halt, Farris fired, and the inquest returned a verdict on those facts.

accounts.label: Bryan Eagle dispatch (shooter's version)
accounts.gist: Jesse Faris, robbed the night before, found a convict in the bushes near the creek and proposed to search him for the stolen property; the man came at him with a razor and Faris shot him.

framing.detail: Under 'Negro Killed by an Officer', the Houston Post relayed the officer's account and the inquest verdict as settled fact.
Under 'Killed an Escaped Convict', the Bryan Eagle framed the dead man by his status as a convict and gave the shooter's version without qualification.

versions.value: Jesse Faris, no official title, the victim of a robbery

conflicts.note: Probably the same man with variant spelling; the papers differ on whether he acted as an officer.
